title: EN 301 549 and the European Accessibility Act: citation status
purpose: Know when conformity with EN 301 549 starts to carry a presumption of conformity under Directive (EU) 2019/882, so that guidance which describes WCAG 2.2 criteria can say correctly whether they are EU legal requirements.

requirements.question: Has a reference to any harmonised standard been published in the Official Journal in support of Directive (EU) 2019/882, the European Accessibility Act?
Which version of EN 301 549 is the harmonised standard under Directive (EU) 2016/2102, and has that changed?
What is the latest published version of EN 301 549, and where is it in its national adoption timetable?
What is the standing of WCAG 2.2 at W3C and at ISO?

indicators.watch_for: A Commission implementing decision that cites a harmonised standard in support of Directive (EU) 2019/882 is published in the Official Journal, L series.
indicators.where: EUR-Lex, and the Commission's harmonised standards index (S2)
indicators.would_mean: Conformity with the cited standard carries a presumption of conformity under the Act from the date the decision applies.

indicators.watch_for: The Commission's harmonised standards index lists an entry for Directive (EU) 2019/882.
indicators.would_mean: A reference has been published or is about to be. Read the decision the entry links to before changing F1 to F4.

indicators.watch_for: The Commission's page for Directive (EU) 2016/2102 lists an amendment to Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/2048 dated after 11 August 2021.
indicators.where: The page for public sector websites and mobile applications (S9)
indicators.would_mean: The harmonised version for public sector websites has changed. Re-read F5 against the new decision.

indicators.watch_for: ETSI's delivery directory for EN 301 549 lists an entry numbered above 04.01.01.
indicators.would_mean: V4.1.1 has been corrected or superseded. Re-read F6 and F8.

indicators.watch_for: W3C's WCAG overview states that ISO/IEC 40500:2026 is published or available.
indicators.would_mean: The ISO edition has caught up with the December 2024 text of WCAG 2.2.

state.statement: A law firm note dated 18 September 2026 says EN 301 549 V4.1.1 is an official European standard whose main legal effect will not occur until it is cited in the Official Journal. On that account it had not been cited by that date.
As of August 2026 no harmonised standard had been cited in the Official Journal in support of Directive (EU) 2019/882.
The Commission's harmonised standards index lists one entry under Accessibility, for websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies, and no entry for Directive (EU) 2019/882.

Whether the Official Journal itself now carries a reference under Directive (EU) 2019/882 is not established. The Official Journal was not searched, and an index page with no entry is not proof that nothing has been published.

EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (2021-03) is the harmonised standard for websites and mobile applications under Directive (EU) 2016/2102, by Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/1339 of 11 August 2021. The Commission's page lists that decision as the only amendment to Implementing Decision (EU) 2018/2048.
The latest published version is EN 301 549 V4.1.1 (2026-09). Its foreword gives 24 August 2026 as the date of adoption, and ETSI's delivery server lists its PDF dated 2 September 2026.
The law firm note says V4.1.1 aligns its web requirements with WCAG 2.2 and adds a compliance framework that maps to the essential requirements of the European Accessibility Act.
The V4.1.1 foreword sets 30 November 2026 as the latest date of announcement, 31 May 2027 for national publication or endorsement, and 31 May 2028 for withdrawal of conflicting national standards.

W3C states that WCAG 2.2 was published on 5 October 2023 and updated on 12 December 2024, that it is approved as ISO/IEC 40500:2025, and that it expects the December 2024 version to be available as ISO/IEC 40500:2026 by late 2026.
Until a reference is cited under Directive (EU) 2019/882, guidance should describe WCAG 2.2 criteria as W3C criteria and not as EU legal requirements. Confidence: moderate, because F4 is open.
